words.gloss: I will not slacken my hand

ai.literal: To do duty, a person, 'I will not slacken my hand', saying, than that greatness, dignity, possessing, there is nothing.
ai.translation: There is no dignity greater than the greatness of a person who says, 'I will not slacken my efforts until my duty is done.'
ai.modern: தன் கடமையைச் செய்ய ஒருவன் 'நான் என் கையைத் தளர்த்த மாட்டேன்' என்று விடாமுயற்சியுடன் கூறும் பெருமையைக் காட்டிலும் மேலான பெருமை வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet praises the relentless determination of an individual dedicated to uplifting their family and community. The phrase 'கைதூவேன்' literally means 'I will not rest my hand' or 'I will not slacken my efforts,' representing tireless work. The poet asserts that there is no greater dignity or nobility ('பீடு') in the world than the greatness ('பெருமை') of possessing such an unwavering attitude towards one's duty ('கருமம்').

ai.literal: And manly effort, and abundant wisdom, called of these two, by the unceasing action, will rise the family.
ai.translation: A family will rise and prosper through the unceasing practice of two qualities: manly effort and mature wisdom.
ai.modern: முயற்சியும் நிறைந்த அறிவும் ஆகிய இவ்விரண்டின் இடைவிடாத செயல்பாட்டினால் ஒருவனுடைய குடி உயர்வடையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet outlines the two essential pillars required to elevate one's family or lineage (குடி). These are active, manly effort (ஆள்வினை) and mature, deep wisdom (ஆன்ற அறிவு). The poet emphasizes that merely possessing these qualities is not enough; they must be put into continuous, unceasing action (நீள்வினை). It is through this sustained application of effort and wisdom that a family's status and honor will grow and rise (நீளும்).

ai.literal: To a person who says 'I will raise my family', the deity, tucking up its garment, will itself go before.
ai.translation: To the person who resolves, 'I will elevate my family,' the divine power will gird up its loins and lead the way.
ai.modern: என் குடியை உயர்த்துவேன் என்று முயலும் ஒருவனுக்கு, தெய்வமே தன் ஆடையைக் கட்டிக்கொண்டு அவனுக்கு முன்னே வந்து உதவி செய்யும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of determination in uplifting one's family or community. When a person takes a firm resolve to work for the elevation of their clan, even the divine power is said to hasten to their aid. The poet uses the vivid image of the deity 'girding up its loins' (tucking up its garment) to show that active, enthusiastic assistance is guaranteed to those who take initiative. It beautifully illustrates that sincere human effort commands divine cooperation.

words.gloss: spontaneously or of its own accord

ai.literal: Without planning, of its own accord, completion will reach, for those who strive without delay for their own family.
ai.translation: For those who strive without delay to elevate their family, success will come spontaneously, even without deliberate planning.
ai.modern: தன் குடும்பத்தை உயர்த்தத் தாமதிக்காமல் உழைப்பவர்களுக்கு, அவர்கள் செய்ய நினைக்கும் காரியங்கள் திட்டமிடாமலேயே தானாகவே வெற்றியை அடையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the power of prompt and dedicated action in uplifting one's family. For those who work tirelessly and without procrastination ('தாழாது உஞற்றுபவர்க்கு') to improve their clan, success comes naturally. The poet suggests that such sincere efforts bear fruit spontaneously ('தானே முடிவு எய்தும்'), even without the need for elaborate or anxious planning ('சூழாமல்'). The momentum of immediate, selfless action itself clears obstacles and ensures success.

parts.gloss: the world or people of the world

ai.literal: Him who lives elevating his family, being free from faults, the world will surround as a kinsman.
ai.translation: The world will gather around as a close relative to embrace the one who lives free of faults, constantly working to elevate their family.
ai.modern: குற்றம் இல்லாதவனாய் தன் குடியை உயரச் செய்து வாழ்கின்றவனை, இவ்வுலகம் தன் உறவினனாகக் கருதிச் சூழ்ந்து கொள்ளும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the universal respect earned by someone who dedicates their life to the upliftment of their family or community through righteous means. The phrase 'kuṟṟam ilaṉāy' emphasizes that this effort must be free of moral blemishes or dishonest deeds. When a person selflessly elevates their lineage ('kuṭi ceytu') with such integrity, they do not remain isolated; instead, the entire world ('ulaku') embraces them. The world treats them not as a stranger, but surrounds them with the warmth and affection reserved for one's own close kin ('cuṟṟamā').

ai.literal: Good manliness is, for a person, making the dignity of the family they were born in, and taking it upon themselves.
ai.translation: True manliness for a person consists in taking upon themselves the responsibility to elevate and lead the family in which they were born.
ai.modern: ஒருவனுக்குச் சிறந்த ஆண்மை என்பது, தான் பிறந்த குடும்பத்தை ஆளும் பொறுப்பை ஏற்று அதை மேம்படுத்துவதாகும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet defines true manliness or noble effort (நல்லாண்மை) not as mere physical strength or individual success, but as the dedication to uplift one's own family. The word 'ஆண்மை' (manliness/strength) is used twice: first as 'நல்லாண்மை' (true/noble effort) and then as 'இல்லாண்மை' (family leadership/management). The poet explains that a person's ultimate strength is demonstrated when they take charge of their family's welfare and elevate its status. This active responsibility (ஆக்கிக் கொளல்) is what constitutes genuine dignity and duty.

ai.literal: Like the brave in the midst of battle, the burden within one's own family is indeed upon those who are capable.
ai.translation: Just as the brunt of a battle falls upon the brave, the burden of sustaining a family rests upon those within it who are capable of bearing it.
ai.modern: போர்க்களத்தில் போரின் பாரம் வீரர்களிடம் இருப்பது போல, ஒரு குடும்பத்திலும் அதைத் தாங்கி நடத்தும் பொறுப்பு, அக்குடும்பத்தில் உள்ள செயல்வல்லமை உடையவர்களிடமே சாரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a powerful analogy from the battlefield to explain family responsibility. In a battle, the actual burden of fighting and securing victory falls upon the brave soldiers who stand firm. Similarly, within a family or community, the heavy responsibility of supporting and elevating the group falls entirely upon those members who are capable and strong enough to bear it. The word 'porai' means burden or weight, signifying the challenges of maintaining a family, and 'āṟṟuvār' refers to those with the strength and capability to act.

ai.literal: To those who elevate their family, there is no proper season; if they practice sloth and consider their pride, it will be ruined.
ai.translation: For those who strive to elevate their family, there is no set season for work; if they indulge in laziness and worry about their personal dignity, their family will go to ruin.
ai.modern: தங்கள் குடும்பத்தை உயரச் செய்ய உழைப்பவர்களுக்குக் குறிப்பிட்ட காலம் என்று எதுவும் இல்லை; அவர்கள் சோம்பல் பட்டுக்கொண்டு, தங்கள் மானத்தைப் பற்றி கவலைப்பட்டுக் கொண்டிருந்தால் குடும்பம் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that uplifting one's family requires constant, selfless effort. Those who are committed to this task cannot wait for a convenient time or a favorable season (paruvam) to act. If they succumb to laziness (mati) or hesitate out of concern for their personal pride and status (manam), their noble purpose will fail and the family will decline. Therefore, overcoming sloth and ego is essential for the welfare of one's lineage.

ai.literal: Is the body of him who shields his family from faults indeed a vessel for receiving affliction?
ai.translation: Is the body of a person who constantly shields their family from faults and ruin merely a vessel destined to hold suffering?
ai.modern: தன் குடும்பத்திற்கு வரும் குற்றங்களை நீக்கப் பாடுபடுபவனுடைய உடம்பு, துன்பங்களை மட்டுமே தாங்கும் ஒரு பாத்திரமோ?
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense self-sacrifice of an individual who dedicates their life to protecting and uplifting their family. Such a person constantly faces hardships and struggles to shield their family from faults and ruin. The poet rhetorically asks if their very body is meant to be a vessel ('kolkalam') solely for containing suffering ('idumbai'), emphasizing that their life is defined by enduring pain for the sake of their family's honor.

ai.literal: When affliction destroys the support, the family that does not have an able person to immediately prop it up will fall.
ai.translation: A family that lacks an able person to immediately prop it up will collapse when affliction destroys its support.
ai.modern: துன்பங்கள் வந்து குடும்பத்தின் தூணை அழிக்கும்போது, அதனைத் தாங்கிப் பிடிக்கும் தகுதியான நபர் இல்லாத குடும்பம் அழிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses the metaphor of a house collapsing when its main pillar is destroyed. Here, the family is compared to a house, and its stability is threatened by affliction, which acts like a force destroying the support. If there is no able person to immediately prop it up, the family will inevitably fall. The poet emphasizes that a family needs an active, capable member who can step in during times of crisis to prevent its ruin.
